content:
Let
\[
S=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac1{10^n-1}.
\]
Using
\[
\frac1{10^n-1}=10^{-n}\sum_{k\ge 0}10^{-kn},
\]
we get
\[
S=\sum_{m\ge 1} d(m)10^{-m},
\]
where \(d(m)\) is the number of positive divisors of \(m\).

Thus
\[
10^{100}S=\sum_{m=1}^{100} d(m)10^{100-m}+\sum_{m\ge 101}d(m)10^{100-m}.
\]
The tail is
\[
\frac{d(101)}{10}+\frac{d(102)}{100}+\frac{d(103)}{1000}+\cdots
=0.2+0.08+0.002+\cdots<1,
\]
so it does not affect the integer part.

Therefore
\[
\left\lfloor 10^{100}S\right\rfloor \equiv 100d(98)+10d(99)+d(100)\pmod{1000}.
\]

Now
\[
d(98)=d(2\cdot 7^2)=6,\quad d(99)=d(3^2\cdot 11)=6,\quad d(100)=d(2^2\cdot 5^2)=9.
\]
So
\[
100(6)+10(6)+9=669.
\]

\[
\boxed{669}
\]
